# keel

> keel turns coding agents into work owners. It is a project-neutral, multi-agent
> workflow backbone that drives a GitHub issue from intake to done: select →
> branch → implement → CI → review → test → merge → close → capture. Projects set
> their values in `project.yaml` and snap their own logic into named extension
> slots. Stdlib-first Python CLI, single runtime dependency, 100% test coverage,
> 16 `/keel` commands. Works across Claude Code, Codex, and Gemini.

## Docs

- [Home](https://berkayturanci.github.io/keel/): overview, positioning, and quick start
- [Documentation](https://berkayturanci.github.io/keel/docs.html): commands, config, extension slots, and the fixed backbone
- [Coverage report](https://berkayturanci.github.io/keel/coverage.html): live test-coverage dashboard

## Source

- [GitHub repository](https://github.com/berkayturanci/keel): source, issues, and releases

## Key concepts

- Fixed backbone: the invariant step sequence every issue flows through
- Project-neutral core: all project specifics live in `project.yaml`, read via the `keel` CLI
- Extension slots: named hooks where a project snaps in its own implementers/reviewers
- Pure-core / thin-I/O split with a strict 100% coverage bar
